## Before you upgrade

- **This is a security release.** It fixes three high and several medium issues found by a red team review of 0.4.1: requests that could use up the server's memory or CPU, and sign-in, ingest, web and archive hardening (see Security fixes). Several changes below need a look before you upgrade.
- **Plain archives need an override while encryption is on.** A plain (unencrypted) archive whose manifest no key of this server authenticates, written before encryption was turned on or by a version before manifests had MACs, is refused while `retention.encrypt_archives` is on. To restore such archives, set `retention.allow_unauthenticated_archives: true` in signalith.yaml, or pass `-allow-unauthenticated` to `signalith archive`. Remove the setting once they are restored. (CRYPTO-01)
- **Encrypted archives need a MAC too, but old ones keep reading.** An encrypted archive's manifest must now carry a MAC, because the file's encryption does not record which day it holds. The first time each server starts this version, it lists the encrypted archives in its archive folder that have no MAC, with their SHA-256, in its state folder (`archive-legacy-<id>.json`). Those keep reading with no setting. An encrypted archive without a MAC that was not in the folder at that first start needs `retention.allow_unauthenticated_archives`. This covers archives copied back in later and folders that were not mounted at the first start. (CRYPTO-01)
- **Master key files that other accounts can read stop the server from starting.** On Linux and other Unix systems, a group-readable, world-readable or foreign-owned master key file now stops `signalith serve`, and the error gives the `chmod` or `chown` fix. Docker, Podman and Kubernetes containers only get a warning. LXC, LXD and Proxmox system containers stop like any other computer; set `SIGNALITH_CONTAINER=1` only if one is really an application container. On Windows, the server stops when the key file's access list lets Everyone, Users, Authenticated Users, Guests, Interactive, Anonymous or Domain Users read or change it, and the error gives the `icacls` fix. (CRYPTO-06)
- **Agent tokens are held to their intake.** The OpenTelemetry (OTLP) intake accepts only tokens made for OpenTelemetry, plus older tokens that have no purpose. The agent intake refuses tokens made for OpenTelemetry or osquery. A refused token gets a `purpose_mismatch` error that says to get a configuration with a token made for that agent from **Add data**. (ING-02..ING-10)
- **`signalith init -admin-password` is refused.** It put the password on the command line. Set `SIGNALITH_NEW_PASSWORD` instead. (AUTHRT-12)
- **Password hashes are made again at bcrypt cost 12.** When a user signs in with a hash made by an older version, the hash is made again, and that ends the user's other sessions once. (AUTHRT-12)
- **The AI model over plain http only reaches local addresses.** A plain `http://` `assistant.url` that names a public IP address turns the AI features off unless `assistant.allow_insecure_http` is on. A host name (`ollama`, `ollama.lan`, `gpu01.corp.example`, `ollama.svc.cluster.local`) keeps the AI on, with a warning. It is checked each time Signalith connects: only this computer and private addresses are reached, and a public address fails with an error that says why. Through `HTTPS_PROXY`, a plain-http model name must resolve on the Signalith server itself. (AI-02)
- **Single sign-on started during a rolling upgrade has to start over once.** The OpenID Connect and SAML sign-in cookies have a new format. A sign-in that was started on a server of the old version and comes back to a server of the new version (or the other way round) fails once, and starting it again works. (AUTHRT-11)
- **Sign-in locks are not shared across versions during a rolling upgrade.** The keys of the sign-in limiter's locks changed. While servers of both versions run, a lock set on one version is not seen by servers of the other until it expires. (RT-01, AUTHRT-02)
- **Splunk anomaly rules add their own risk score.** Their score was not read, so every anomaly added the default 25. Risk totals and risk-based findings may change. (SRCH-212)
- **Behind a reverse proxy, keep the Host header or set `server.public_url`.** Signalith checks that a sign-in or other change comes from its own page. It now also accepts an `Origin` equal to `server.public_url`, so proxies that rewrite `Host` keep working. The nginx example in the HTTPS docs now uses `proxy_set_header Host $http_host;` (keeps the port) instead of `$host`. (WEB-03)

## Security fixes

- **Origin check behind proxies.** An `Origin` equal to `server.public_url`'s origin is accepted whatever `Host` the proxy sends. Before, a proxy that dropped the port from `Host` (nginx `$host`) or sent its upstream address (`127.0.0.1:9000`) refused every sign-in. (WEB-03)
- **Built-in admin rename no longer reverts changes.** When the old document of a built-in admin rename changed during the rename, only the fields that changed on it are carried over. Before, the whole document was copied, which reverted a password or two-step change made under the new name. (AUTHRT-10)
- **Shared addresses no longer lock out known users.** The failure ceiling of a shared address (proxy or NAT) no longer applies to a known browser, or to an account that was already signed in to through that address with its current password. Past the ceiling, attempts are spaced out to the ceiling's rate instead of being refused for the rest of the minute. One person's made-up names can no longer keep everyone behind the address out. (RT-01, AUTHRT-02)
- **AI model requests through a proxy check the model's host.** With `HTTPS_PROXY` set, the model's host is resolved and checked before the proxy is used, so a model address cannot point a proxy at a cloud metadata service. Google Cloud's IPv6 metadata address (`fd20:ce::254`) and Alibaba Cloud's (`100.100.100.200`) are now blocked as well. (AI-03)
- **Archives cannot be swapped between days.** An encrypted archive's file and manifest can no longer be copied over another day's: encrypted manifests must carry a MAC, except old ones listed at the upgrade. (CRYPTO-01)
- **Sign-in timing no longer reveals dormant users.** An unknown user name is checked at one of the bcrypt costs of the stored hashes, chosen by the name. Users who have not signed in since their hash was made at cost 10 can no longer be told apart from names that do not exist. (AUTHRT-12)
- **Failed sign-ins stay within the audit caps.** Only the failure that starts a lock or slow-down skips the caps. Before, every failure on an account that was slowed down did. A wrong two-step code after a right password has an audit budget of its own, so floods of wrong passwords cannot hide it. (AUTHRT-02, AUTHRT-03)
- **What the sealed OpenID Connect cookie protects against.** The MAC refuses forged cookies. Login CSRF with a planted genuine cookie is stopped by the `__Host-` prefix over HTTPS. Over plain HTTP nothing can stop it, so use HTTPS for single sign-on. (AUTHRT-11)
- **Public demo: room for new visitors.** For the share of demo sign-ins kept for new visitors, an IPv6 /48 counts as one visitor. Visitors through a shared address, or whose address can't be determined, never count as new. (AUTHRT-05)
- **API tokens kept after a user loses access are named.** When SCIM provisioning or the directory turns off or deletes a user, the audit log names the API tokens that user made that keep working. (AUTHRT-09)
- **Detection runs count toward the search limits.** Detection test, backtest and run on demand now count toward the per-user search rate and in-flight limits. A search response is never cut off partway because JSON escaping made it larger. (RT-02)
- **Searches have firmer limits.** A user's search result is capped at 128 MB and streamed row by row, searches get a per-user rate limit and a limit on how many run at once, and regular expressions are charged for their work before they run, so a slow one is refused. A small search can no longer hold gigabytes or a CPU for seconds. (RT-02, RT-03, SRCH-03, SRCH-04)
- **The sign-in limiter's memory is bounded.** User names and passwords longer than any account's are refused before the limiter, which keeps only a digest of each name and forgets old entries. A stream of made-up names can no longer fill the server's memory. Failed sign-ins and other refusals share an audit budget with one summary record. (RT-01, AUTHRT-02, AUTHRT-04)
- **Events name the computer key that sent them.** Events from the agent carry the computer key that sent them and are marked when the computer name in an event does not match that key, so one computer's token can no longer quietly write events as another. OTLP counts split events against the record cap before writing. (ING-02 to ING-10)
- **Break-glass sign-in asks for the two-step code.** The password from `signalith passwd -local` skipped two-step sign-in; while the built-in admin's authenticator app can still be read, its code is now asked for, and the audit record says `break_glass`. (AUTHRT-06)
- **Demo visitors and tenants see less.** The demo visitor's reads are audited like its searches and it sees only the default tenant; a tenant's analyst can no longer tell which user names exist in other tenants from the case owner field. (AUTHZ-01 to AUTHZ-05)
- **Playbooks start for hand-raised findings only when named.** A finding raised by hand no longer starts every "any detection" playbook on the entities typed into it. (AUTHZ-04)
- **AI hardening.** A benign verdict from Investigate with AI on data that looked like instructions carries a caution, model-written Ask queries with `map`, `join`, `append`, `union` or subsearches wait for the analyst to run them, and model addresses with `?`, `#` or link-local and metadata hosts are refused. (AI-01, AI-03, AI-04)
- **The sign-in page no longer names the exact version.** The web page's files are named by an opaque build token and the version header is sent only to signed-in users. A path after sign-in is cleaned before it is checked, CSV export guards joined multivalue cells, and ending a session clears that user's stored page state. (WEB-01, WEB-02, WEB-05, WEB-06, WEB-10)
- **Removing a cluster server warns about OpenSearch's CA key.** Every member can read it, so `remove` and `leave` say how to replace it, and `signalith opensearch-ca import` can now replace the cluster's CA. `join` warns when its token is given on the command line. (CRYPTO-02, CRYPTO-05)

## What's new

- **Data sources page.** Every host and source type that sent events in the last 7 days, with its status (sending, quiet, stopped), events per minute, and how the last hour compares with its usual hour, so a source that stopped or changed sharply stands out. Health and the posture dashboard link to it.
- **Share detections.** Export downloads every detection made here as one YAML file, turned off; Import rule reads that file, one detection or a Sigma rule, and adds the chosen rules turned off.
- **Notify from a detection.** Each detection shows which notification rules send its findings, with a shortcut to add one. A case's timeline can be filtered to notes, files, searches and other kinds.
- **Optional AI first pass over new findings.** Off by default. When an admin turns it on, the model looks at each new finding of enough urgency with one round of searches and keeps its verdict and summary on the finding as a suggestion. It never changes status or owner, skips sample data and stops at a daily limit.
- **Single sign-on can require the provider's second factor.** `auth.oidc.require_mfa` checks the ID token's `amr` claim and `auth.saml.mfa_context` asks for and requires an authentication context. Both are off by default. (AUTH-209)

## Fixes

- Pack rules that read Security events Windows does not audit by default carry a `needs-audit-policy` tag on Browse rules and count as dark on the pack card. (SRCH-213)
- The Security page says when an install from before 0.4.0 still has the snapshot role mapped while scheduled snapshots are off, with the command to remove it. (DEP-209)
- With cold storage on, the Docker quick start's `snapshot.sh backups` works again.
- On Windows, saving an asset list while it is being read is retried instead of failing.
- The container image's Debian base is refreshed.
- Releases are built only from a commit on `main` whose CI passed. (CI-205)
